abstract: Appropriate axon diameters are crucial for establishing conduction speeds that support neural circuit function, yet regulation of axon diameter remains poorly understood despite over 100-fold variation across neurons. In the CNS, large-calibre axons are myelinated, and axon diameter changes following demyelination or disruption of myelin-associated proteins suggest a role for myelin in regulating axon diameter; however, whether these changes reflect a developmental requirement for myelin in establishing axon diameter or a secondary pathology remains unclear. Here, we examined developmental axon diameter growth in the absence of myelination across zebrafish CNS neurons with axons that grow to distinct diameters. We find no difference in the initial establishment of diameters for Mauthner (∼4.0 μm), MiM1 (∼1.3 μm) and CoPA (∼0.8 μm) axons with and without myelin; however, CoPA axons exhibited subtle differences during later diameter refinement. In mice, optic nerve axons in unmyelinated postnatal day 14 Myrffl/fl;Olig2cre mutants and postnatal day 75 Mbpshi/shi mice lacking compact myelin also achieved normal and diverse (∼9-fold range) diameters. Together, these findings show that developmental diameter growth of many CNS axons occurs largely independently of myelination.
